title: Build a boat
intro: Design a small floating boat that can carry a cargo of coins.

steps.title: Shape a hull
steps.text: Fold a sheet of foil into a shallow boat with a flat bottom and raised sides.

steps.title: Test it
steps.text: Place the boat on the water. Does it float without leaking?

steps.title: Load the cargo
steps.text: Add coins one at a time, spreading them evenly. Count how many the boat carries before sinking.

steps.title: Improve the design
steps.text: Build a wider or longer boat. Test it again with the same coins.

challenge: Which shape carries the most cargo? Why do you think that is?
safety: Use a shallow basin with an adult nearby. Dry any spilled water.

title: Build a bridge
intro: Discover how the shape of paper changes its strength.

steps.title: Make a gap
steps.text: Place the books about 15 cm apart.

steps.title: Test a flat sheet
steps.text: Lay one sheet across the gap. Add coins in the centre until the bridge bends.

steps.title: Change its shape
steps.text: Fold a new sheet into an accordion shape and place it across the same gap.

steps.title: Compare
steps.text: Count how many coins each bridge can carry. Try another fold.

challenge: Can you make a stronger bridge using only one sheet of paper?
safety: Keep the bridge low and use only small loads.

title: Grow a bean
intro: Watch a seed develop roots, a stem and leaves.

steps.title: Prepare the seed
steps.text: Put damp paper towel inside the cup and place the bean where you can see it.

steps.title: Choose a place
steps.text: Put the cup in a warm spot with indirect light. Keep the towel damp, not flooded.

steps.title: Observe
steps.text: Check the seed each day. Draw or describe the first root and the emerging shoot.

steps.title: Plant it
steps.text: When roots and a shoot have developed, ask an adult to help move it into soil.

challenge: Which appeared first, the root or the shoot? How does the plant change over a week?
safety: Do not eat the seed or sprouts. Wash your hands after handling soil.

title: Make a sundial
intro: Use the changing position of a shadow to investigate time.

steps.title: Set up the dial
steps.text: Stand the pencil upright in clay on the cardboard. Put it on a flat sunny surface.

steps.title: Mark the shadow
steps.text: Trace the shadow and write the current time beside the line.

steps.title: Return later
steps.text: Repeat every hour while the sun is shining. Do not move the cardboard.

steps.title: Compare
steps.text: Look at how the shadow's direction and length changed.

challenge: When was the shadow shortest? What might happen tomorrow?
safety: Never look directly at the sun. Use sun protection outside.

title: Make a wind indicator
intro: Build a simple instrument to observe wind direction.

steps.title: Attach the ribbon
steps.text: Tie the ribbon to one end of the stick with string.

steps.title: Find a clear space
steps.text: Hold the stick upright outdoors, away from buildings and trees.

steps.title: Observe the wind
steps.text: Watch which direction the ribbon points. It points downwind.

steps.title: Record changes
steps.text: Repeat in the morning and afternoon. Draw the ribbon's direction and compare.

challenge: Does the wind always come from the same direction?
safety: Stay away from roads and power lines. Do not use it in a storm.
